items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: George Shearing gave me my first job in New York when I was about eighteen... So he gave me two nights.

ctx.x: And three years later you were out?

Three years later I was on the road playing with professional bands. That’s a true story, yeah. George Shearing gave me my first job in New York when I was about eighteen. I was sitting in with Bud Powell and he played “Cherokee” for twenty-five minutes, and I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

stayed with it. And George Shearing said anyone that could play “Cherokee” at that tempo for twenty-five minutes, I’m going to give a gig to. This is just what he said. And his manager came over and said “Mr. Shearing wants to talk to you.” And he says “young man, anybody that can play ‘Cherokee’ for twenty-five minutes with Bud Powell, I’ve got to give a job to.” I thought it was so sweet the way he did it. And he says “besides, my drummer is a little hung up” you know he said later. So he gave me two nights.…

items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: His dynamic playing and vivacious personality have sparked the bands of Jack Teagarden, Benny Goodman, Duke Ellington and George Shearing.

ctx.x: Ed Shaughnessy may be the most recognized drummer in the country. His dynamic playing and vivacious personality have sparked the bands of Jack Teagarden, Benny Goodman, Duke Ellington and George Shearing. A native of Jersey City, Ed’s first playing experience was in the clubs of the flourishing jazz scene on New York’s 52nd Street. Ed was interviewed in Clinton, New York on April 25, 1998 by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
